freshProfileReplication.conclusion: The observed Firefox UA setup does not provide one unique visitor ID per fresh profile.

limits: Shows recognition follows the selected persistent WebKit store in this test.
Does not locate the precise persisted signal or reveal the server matching algorithm.
A fresh UUID store alone does not guarantee a different Fingerprint visitor ID.
Three retained historical IDs do not imply one ID per newly created profile.
The tested clearing/restart combinations identify causal groups, not every internal WebKit or server signal.
Build23 restart observations used abrupt process termination. Later tests found unflushed fresh data can be lost; network-only claims require the new persistence checks.

Build26 cold-copy observations had native disk-cache records reappear after restart. These were not accepted as clean token-sufficiency proofs. Build28 source review found disk-cache enumeration can span network sessions, so these records alone do not prove target-store contamination.
A build26 localStorage-copy cohort had a missing Worker UA observation and is excluded from strict totals.
No engine, response, DOM visitor ID, SDK event, or provider matching result was forged.
Native record enumeration timeouts are unknown metadata, never evidence that a store is empty.
Build28 Chrome/native seeded empty controls converged with the source ID even when target-first; the earlier build27 order-dependent contrast did not replicate under the new measurement protocol.
Additional UA families produced four new IDs, but repeating the exact Edge/Opera seeds in fresh stores reused their earlier IDs. Seven retained profiles are not a per-UUID uniqueness guarantee.
A native DiskCache record list can cover multiple network sessions; compare actual target-directory inventories before attributing cache to one profile.

finalPreservedSevenProfileRecheck.limit: These are seven retained profile histories, not one new ID for each newly created UUID.

sourceSeparatedCookieTransferContrast.limit: A sufficient cookie transfer in this measured condition does not establish every retention path or unique IDs for every new profile.

nativeCacheEnumerationScope.finding: Disk-cache enumeration in fetchWebsiteData loops over every network session in the process. Native DiskCache records are not sufficient to attribute files to the requested store.
nativeCacheEnumerationScope.limitation: Related open-source tag inspected, not disassembly of the exact device binary; actual per-store file inventories are measured separately.

prospectiveVersionSeedCollisionTests.limit: Only measured IDs can be compared. UA variation and store UUIDs cannot guarantee a third-party provider will assign a new ID.

sourceSeparatedStateResetControls.limit: These are removal-group controls on disposable stores; they do not identify every server or WebKit retention mechanism.
